title.narrative: Drought Emergency Response in the Borana Zone (DERB)

description.narrative: Ethiopia is a landlocked country. It is divided into 11 regions and two city administrations under these regions, plenty of zones, districts, and kebeles are structured for administration purposes. The country has more than eighty ethnic diversities with about 120 million people. Of the total population, 50% are female and 50% are male with a 2.6% annual population growth rate. About 42% of the population is under 15 years of age. Eighty-three percent live in rural areas and depend on rainfed agriculture for their livelihoods. Eight-seven percent of the population is “multidimensionally poor”, suffering from some combination of food insecurity, insufficient access to adequate education and health services, and inadequate employment opportunities. These challenges are due, to climate shocks (mainly drought and floods), to conflict, war, insecurity and disease outbreaks coupled with a deteriorating economy. Consequently, humanitarian and development situations in almost all parts of Ethiopia are deteriorating. Drought has mainly affected people living in the southern, southeastern, and eastern parts of the country. According to UNICEF Ethiopia Appeal 2023, at least 31.4 million people, including 16.5 million children, 7.8 million women, and 5.7 million people with disabilities are suffering due to multiple, overlapping hazards: severe drought, flooding, conflict, armed conflict, inter-communal violence, and outbreaks of diseases including cholera, measles, and malaria. In the southern and eastern regions of the country (in the Oromia, Afar, Somali, and Southern Nations, Nationalities and Peoples Regions. The worst drought in 40 years has impacted 24.1 million people where more than 3.5 million livestock have died, and the livelihoods of pastoralists and agro-pastoralists have been extinguished. Families have been forced to migrate in search of food and pasture, forcing children to drop out of school and increasingly face child marriage as the only prospect for a family's survival. An IPC classification of 4 (emergency levels) is indicated in all affected regions through January 2023. Recent ‘Find and Treat’ nutrition campaigns have shown a proxy global acute malnutrition mean average of 23 percent in the drought-affected regions, exceeding the global emergency threshold of 15 percent. Southern Ethiopia part, particularly, Boren zone(almost all districts) has been severely affected by the drought impact. It caused water scarcity, food insecurity, and severe disruption to livelihoods. It is resulting in rising food prices, increasing malnutrition rates amongst children, and displacement of people searching for food and pastures. If not addressed, the drought may lead to famine-like conditions. Drying or low-quality water sources also increase the risk of diseases. As these assessments from zone sectors demonstrate, the current drought is the worst seen in a generation. With a grim weather outlook for the March to May main rainy season, the zone is likely heading towards the fourth consecutive seasonal failure. Taking this severe drought into consideration, Cordaid, EECMY DASSC, and HUNDEE have planned a response project through financial support from Kia and Cordaid global office.

title.narrative: Food & Nutrition Security Corporate Indicators
Number of people with improved food security

description.narrative: Number of households with an improved score on the household food insecurity access scale (HFIAS) compared to the baseline score. This score is a household score and needs to be translated to the number of individual household members (based on average household size)

title.narrative: Number of women with diversified diets

description.narrative: Individual dietary diversity scores aim to reflect nutrient adequacy. Studies in different age groups have shown that an increase in individual dietary diversity score is related to increased nutrient adequacy of the diet. Dietary diversity scores have been validated for several age/sex groups as proxy measures for macro and/ or micronutrient adequacy of the diet. Number of women with an improved dietary diversity, as shown by an improved score on the Minimum Dietary Diversity for Women (MDD-W) compared to the baseline. It can be used as a proxy indicator for nutrition adequacy and quality of food for the whole household by multiplying the number of women with scoring in a certain category with the average or actual household size.

title.narrative: Climate Resilience
The project integrates climate risks in programming

description.narrative: The integration of climate risks in programming includes an undertaking of concrete actions to reduce and/or mitigate risks related to climate change impact and disaster risks ( for example droughts, erosion, salinization, flooding, etc.) The projects we refer to could be on the themes of health education, justice, security, disaster management, finance and livelihoods.

title.narrative: Output KRIs - RI
DRR-R6: Number of people whose livelihoods and assets are protected from shocks and stresses

description.narrative: This refers to activities having a direct and short- to medium-term effect on people’s socio-economic wellbeing, aiming to help people protect, increase or diversify their sources of income, and prevent negative coping strategies. Livelihood assets include human, social, physical, natural and financial capital both tangible and intangible (e.g. claims, access).
